items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: the position of piano with Clark Terry and Bob Brookmeyer was open and he got me that, and that became two and a half years

ctx.x: And ’63, early 60s you started getting out with some of the well known names.

Well I arrived in New York in 1960. Here’s an interesting story. I arrived, and the first night I meet Bill Takas, the bass player. And he takes me to the Five Spot and introduces me to Jimmy Giuffre. I sit in with Jimmy Giuffre and I’m actually offered the job on bass. Now as it turns out, I didn’t take it obviously. The next group he had was Paul Bley and Steve Swallow. And that was, he wanted a band of composers. That happened to me twice. The other person it happened with was Maynard Ferguson, who actually…
Clark’s a great fellow to work with I would imagine.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think Roger Kellaway on piano, and me and Bob.

ctx.x: The Half Note. I keep mixing the Half Note and the Blue Note. Yeah, the Half Note. Zoot [Sims] and Al [Cohn] had formed a group. A couple of other people had formed a group. Phil and Quill, Gene Quill and Phil Woods. So we formed a group, CTBB. Our first group, I think we had Bill Crow on – no, maybe we had Joe Benjamin and Osie Johnson, and I think Roger Kellaway on piano, and me and Bob. The personnel didn’t change a heck of a lot. We had – at one time we had Joe Benjamin on bass. One time we had Bill Crow on…
